findings.fix: Collect the house number and street together in one address-line field.
findings.violation: The house number has its own field separate from the street, and it is required, so an address with no number cannot be entered.

findings.fix: Replace it with the standard token for this field, for example email.
findings.violation: The autocomplete value e-mail is not a valid autofill detail in the HTML standard, so autofill is broken for this field.

findings.evidence: The form's heading is 'Create your account' and its submit button reads 'Submit', yet it requires: #website-input (Company website), #member-input (Membership number, 8 digits), #acctnum-input (Account number), #shipspeed-select (Preferred shipping speed), #legalname-input (Your name, labelled identically in purpose to #name-input's Full name), #org-input (Organization name) and #contacttime-input (Preferred contact time), plus the required #hear-select (How did you hear about us).
findings.fix: Drop Preferred shipping speed, Preferred contact time and How did you hear about us from account creation and ask them later if needed; remove the duplicate Your name field; and make Company website, Organization name, Membership number and Account number optional or move them behind a separate business-account path, so creating a personal account needs only name, email, password and a deliverable address.
findings.violation: Roughly half of this account-creation form's required fields serve no part of the stated task: a shipping-speed preference and a preferred contact time both belong to a later interaction, not account creation; how did you hear about us answers nothing the task uses; a company website and an organization name fit a business signup the heading never names; and the Your name field asks again for the name #name-input already collected under Full name. A person must supply or invent answers to all of them before an account exists.

findings.evidence: <button id="viewdetails-btn" type="button" style="padding:12px 20px;font-size:16px">View details</button> sits between the row-contacttime field and the row-hear field, while the primary action, <button id="submit-btn" type="submit">, carries no style attribute at all.
findings.fix: Move View details out of the field sequence, for example into the page header, and give the Submit button at least as much visual weight as View details so the primary action is the most prominent control on the page.
findings.violation: An unrelated secondary action is styled more prominently (explicit padding and font size) than the form's own primary submit button, and it interrupts the column of fields before the last required field instead of sitting where the fields end, so a person moving through the form meets the more visually prominent control first and may mistake it for how to proceed.

findings.fix: Label the button with the action it performs, such as Create account or Send message.
findings.violation: The form's primary button is labelled Submit, a generic word that says nothing about what pressing it does.
On this name field, autocorrection and spellchecking stay on, so a phone keyboard can change a value it does not know.

findings.fix: Remove the confirmation field and offer a control that shows the password as typed.
findings.violation: The form asks for the new password a second time to confirm it, doubling the typing for every person.
